65972-the-plague-of-athens-which-hapned-.creator: Unknown
65972-the-plague-of-athens-which-hapned-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Though it must be said, that the _Historian_ had a vast advantage over the _Poet_; He having been present on the place, and assaulted by the disease himself, had the horror familiar to his Eyes, and all the shapes of the _misery_ still remaining on his mind, which must needs make a great impression on his Pen and Fancie.

arxiv-1910-11566.title: Electromagnetic fault injection against a System-on-Chip, toward new micro-architectural fault models
arxiv-1910-11566.creator: Thomas Trouchkine, Sébanjila Kevin Bukasa, Mathieu Escouteloup, Ronan Lashermes, Guillaume Bouffard
arxiv-1910-11566.description: Abstract Electromagnetic fault injection (EMFI) is a well known technique used to disturb the behaviour of a chip for weakening its security. These attacks are mostly done on simple microcontrollers. On these targets, the fault effects are relatively simple and understood.

arxiv-2011-04194.title: LADA : Look-Ahead Data Acquisition via Augmentation for Active Learning
arxiv-2011-04194.creator: Yoon-Yeong Kim, Kyungwoo Song, JoonHo Jang, Il-Chul Moon
arxiv-2011-04194.description: Abstract Active learning effectively collects data instances for training deep learning models when the labeled dataset is limited and the annotation cost is high. Besides active learning, data augmentation is also an effective technique to enlarge the limited amount of labeled instances.

arxiv-2105-00471.title: Multi-Level Over-the-Air Aggregation of Mobile Edge Computing over D2D Wireless Networks
arxiv-2105-00471.creator: Feng Wang, and Vincent K. N. Lau
arxiv-2105-00471.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Feng Wang, and Vincent K. N. Lau. In this paper, we consider a wireless multihop device-to-device (D2D) based mobile edge computing (MEC) system, where the destination wireless device (WD) is scheduled to compute nomographic functions. Under the MapReduce framework and motivated by reducing communication resource overhead, we propose a new multi-level over-the-air (OTA) aggregation scheme for the destination WD to collect the individual partially aggregated intermediate values (IVAs) for reduction from multiple source WDs in the data shuffling phase.

arxiv-2112-14001.title: Local well-posedness of the capillary-gravity water waves with acute contact angles
arxiv-2112-14001.creator: Mei Ming, Chao Wang, [2mm] School of Mathematics and Statistics,Yunnan University, Kunming 615000, P.R.China [2mm] E-mail: mingmei@ynu.edu.cn, [2mm] School of Mathematical Science, Peking University, Beijing 100871, P.R.China [2mm] E-mail: wangchao@math.pku.edu.cn
arxiv-2112-14001.description: Abstract We consider the two-dimensional capillary-gravity water waves problem where the free surface Γ t \Gamma_{t} intersects the bottom Γ b \Gamma_{b} at two contact points. In our previous works [ 52 , 53 ] , the local well-posedness for this problem has been proved with the contact angles less than π / 16 \pi/16 .

arxiv-2305-03623.title: Optimizing Hyperparameters with Conformal Quantile Regression
arxiv-2305-03623.creator: David Salinas, Jacek Golebiowski, Aaron Klein, Matthias Seeger, Cedric Archambeau
arxiv-2305-03623.description: Abstract Many state-of-the-art hyperparameter optimization (HPO) algorithms rely on model-based optimizers that learn surrogate models of the target function to guide the search. Gaussian processes are the de facto surrogate model due to their ability to capture uncertainty but they make strong assumptions about the observation noise, which might not be warranted in practice.

arxiv-2311-06296.title: Einstein locality: An ignored core element of quantum mechanics
arxiv-2311-06296.creator: Sheng Feng
arxiv-2311-06296.description: Abstract Quantum mechanics is commonly accepted as a complete theory thanks to experimental tests of non-locality based on Bell’s theorem. However, we discover that the completeness of the quantum theory practically suffered from detrimental ignorance of a core element — Einstein locality. Without this element, important experimental results of relevance could hardly receive full understanding or were even completely misinterpreted.

arxiv-2403-06283.title: f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) Analogue Gravity in ( 2 + 1 ) (2+1) D graphene sheet
arxiv-2403-06283.creator: M. Lapola, L. A. Barreiro
arxiv-2403-06283.description: Abstract We examine the analogue gravity model within the context of f(R,T) gravity applied to graphene. The derivation of the Lagrangian density in two dimensions (2D) is undertaken, accounting for the altered gravitational effects as characterized by the function f(R,T).

arxiv-2410-14749.title: CFTS-GAN: Continual Few-Shot Teacher Student for Generative Adversarial Networks
arxiv-2410-14749.creator: Munsif Ali, Leonardo Rossi, Massimo Bertozzi
arxiv-2410-14749.description: Abstract Few-shot and continual learning face two well-known challenges in GANs: overfitting and catastrophic forgetting. Learning new tasks results in catastrophic forgetting in deep learning models. In the case of a few-shot setting, the model learns from a very limited number of samples (e.g. 10 samples), which can lead to overfitting and mode collapse.

arxiv-2503-05562.title: On graph classes with constant domination-packing ratio
arxiv-2503-05562.creator: Marthe Bonamy, Mónika Csikós, Anna Gujgiczer, Yelena Yuditsky
arxiv-2503-05562.description: Abstract The dominating number γ ⁡ ( G ) \gamma(G) of a graph G G is the minimum size of a vertex set whose closed neighborhood covers all the vertices of the graph. The packing number ρ ⁡ ( G ) \rho(G) of G G is the maximum size of a vertex set whose closed neighborhoods are pairwise disjoint.

arxiv-2505-01803.title: Switched Systems Control via Discreteness-Promoting Regularization
arxiv-2505-01803.creator: Masaaki Nagahara, Takuya Ikeda, Ritsuki Hoshimoto
arxiv-2505-01803.description: Abstract This paper proposes a novel method for designing finite-horizon discrete-valued switching signals in linear switched systems based on discreteness-promoting regularization. The inherent combinatorial optimization problem is reformulated as a continuous optimization problem with a non-convex regularization term that promotes discreteness of the control.

arxiv-2508-07075.title: Surgical Knowledge Rewrite in Compact LLMs: An ’Unlearn-then-Learn’ Strategy with ((IA) 3 ) for Localized Factual Modulation and Catastrophic Forgetting Mitigation
arxiv-2508-07075.creator: Stanley Ngugi
arxiv-2508-07075.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle with dynamic knowledge updates, especially when new information conflicts with deeply embedded facts. Such conflicting factual edits often lead to two critical issues: resistance to adopting the new fact and severe catastrophic forgetting of unrelated knowledge.

arxiv-2601-00146.title: Combining datasets with different ground truths using Low-Rank Adaptation to generalize image-based CNN models for photometric redshift prediction
arxiv-2601-00146.creator: Vikram Seenivasan vikrams25@ucla.edu, Srinath Saikrishnan srinathsai22@ucla.edu, Andrew Lizarraga andrewlizarraga@ucla.edu, Jonathan Soriano jsoriano@astro.ucla.edu, Bernie Boscoe boscoeb@sou.edu, Tuan Do tdo@astro.ucla.edu
arxiv-2601-00146.description: Abstract In this work, we demonstrate how Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can be used to combine different galaxy imaging datasets to improve redshift estimation with CNN models for cosmology. LoRA is an established technique for large language models that adds adapter networks to adjust model weights and biases to efficiently fine-tune large base models without retraining.

europmc-pmc5171767.title: Estimating the volume and age of water stored in global lakes using a geo-statistical approach.
europmc-pmc5171767.creator: Messager ML, Lehner B, Grill G, Nedeva I, Schmitt O.
europmc-pmc5171767.description: Lakes are key components of biogeochemical and ecological processes, thus knowledge about their distribution, volume and residence time is crucial in understanding their properties and interactions within the Earth system. However, global information is scarce and inconsistent...

pmc-10484181.title: Purine and purinergic receptors in health and disease
pmc-10484181.creator: Yanling Ai, Hengyi Wang, Lu Liu, Yulin Qi, Shiyun Tang, Jianyuan Tang, Nianzhi Chen
pmc-10484181.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Purines and purinergic receptors are widely distributed throughout the human body. Purine molecules within cells play crucial roles in regulating energy metabolism and other cellular processes, while extracellular purines transmit signals through specific purinergic receptors. The ubiquitous purinergic signaling maintains normal neural excitability, digestion and absorption, respiratory movement, and other complex physiological activities, and participates in cell proliferation, differentiation, migration, and death. Pathological dysregulation of purinergic signaling can result in the development of various diseases, including neurodegeneration, inflammatory reactions, and malignant tumors.

pmc-11625437.title: Mapping Knowledge Landscapes and Evolving Trends of Clinical Hypnotherapy Practice: A Bibliometrics-Based Visualization Analysis
pmc-11625437.creator: Fei-Yi Zhao, Li Li, Peijie Xu, Gerard A Kennedy, Zhen Zheng, Yan-Mei Wang, Wen-Jing Zhang, Li-Ping Yue, Yuen-Shan Ho, Qiang-Qiang Fu, Russell Conduit
pmc-11625437.description: Background and AimsIncreasing interest in hypnotherapy’s application for a wide range of health conditions has spurred a rise in global research and publications. This study aims to visualize development patterns and current research hotspots in clinical hypnotherapy practice using scientometric methods, and to predict future research directions based on the keyword trending topics analysis.

pmc-11678714.title: Intra- and Interpopulation Diversity of the Phytopathogenic Fungi of the Microdochium nivale Species
pmc-11678714.creator: Olga A. Gogoleva, Egor A. Ryazanov, Guzalia Sh. Murzagulova, Sergey N. Ponomarev, Inna B. Chastukhina, Ildar T. Sakhabutdinov, Elena V. Osipova, Gulnaz S. Mannapova, Viktor N. Korzun, Mira L. Ponomareva, Vladimir Yu. Gorshkov
pmc-11678714.description: Our study investigates the intra- and interpopulation diversity of phytopathogenic fungi, using Microdochium nivale as a model organism. A total of 136 strains, representing two populations, were collected from different winter cereal crops (rye, wheat, and triticale) across two agrocenoses. In these strains, we analyzed and compared genetic and phenotypic traits, exploring potential relationships between them.

pmc-12783121.title: New insights into the mechanism of microvascular rarefaction via endothelial-mesenchymal transition in steroid-induced osteonecrosis of femoral head
pmc-12783121.creator: Xiaoqiang Yang, Peng Yang, Jiaru Liao, Fan Yang, Mincong He, Ziqi Li, Qiushi Wei, Wei He
pmc-12783121.description: This study aimed to investigate the potential role of endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) in steroid-induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head (SONFH), evaluate its association with microvascular rarefaction and tissue damage, and preliminarily explore whether glucocorticoid-induced oxidative stress may be involved in this process. A combination of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), in vitro experiments, and animal models were employed.

pmc-12853925.title: Tools and methods for assessing the usability and related aspects of usability of extended reality and telerehabilitation technologies in stroke rehabilitation: a scoping review
pmc-12853925.creator: Fatimata Ouédraogo, Marika Demers, Karla Vanessa Rodrigues Soares Menezes, David Labbé, Karina Lebel, Simon Brière, Mindy F Levin, Michel Tousignant, Dahlia Kairy
pmc-12853925.description: PurposeExtended reality (XR) and telerehabilitation (TR) technologies are increasingly being used into stroke rehabilitation. These technologies have the potential to enhance therapy intensity, motivate users through engaging and interactive environments, and improve access to rehabilitation services in both clinical and home settings. Usability assessment is essential to ensure effective, engaging, and accessible interventions.

pmc-13261581.title: Multi-Pattern Generalization in CO2‑EOR: Physically Consistent Surrogate for Saturation-Field Evolution
pmc-13261581.creator: Junwei Zhao, Yukun Dong, Jiyuan Zhang, Kuankuan Wu
pmc-13261581.description: Accurate and efficient forecasting of CO2 saturation-field evolution is essential for screening injection–production strategies in CO2-EOR/CCUS, yet conventional simulators are too expensive for rapid multiscenario evaluation and many data-driven models generalize poorly across well-pattern topologies. To bridge these gaps, we propose a multimodal, physics-constrained, generative spatiotemporal network (MPG-STNet).

pmc-13317608.title: Endoplasmic Reticulum Geometry Dictates Neuronal Bursting via Calcium Store Refill Rates and Exposes Selective Neuronal Vulnerability
pmc-13317608.creator: Valentina Davi, Pierre Parutto, Yuyi Zhang, Tasuku Konno, Cecile Crapart, Raquel Pereira, John P. Franklin, Mosab Ali Awadelkareem, Daniel C Maddison, Michael J. Devine, Edgar R. Gomes, Joseph Chambers, Elena Koslover, Edward Avezov
pmc-13317608.description: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER)’s continuous morphology is tightly controlled by ER‐shaping proteins, whose genetic or expression defects drive a spectrum of neurodegenerative disorders from Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia to Alzheimer's disease. Why perturbations in ER morphology manifest specifically in neurons remains unknown.

pmc-13452112.title: Epigenetic modulation of the JAK2-STAT3 signaling pathway in osteoporosis: non-coding RNA networks as therapeutic targets
pmc-13452112.creator: Pengjun Wang, Lu Xia, Xiaobin Shang
pmc-13452112.description: BackgroundOsteoporosis, a prevalent metabolic bone disease affects over 200 million people worldwide and is associated with an elevated fracture risk, is characterized by an imbalance between bone resorption and formation. The JAK2–STAT3 signaling pathway serves as a critical regulator of bone remodeling, but its chronic activation contributes to pathological bone metabolism in osteoporosis.

pmc-13677744.title: Cause-of-death data series to monitor cause-specific mortality across time and space
pmc-13677744.creator: Magali Barbieri, France Meslé, Svitlana Poniakina, Denys Dukhovnov, Domantas Jasilionis, Lisa Koerber, Dmitri Jdanov
pmc-13677744.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cause-specific mortality provides useful clues regarding the driving forces behind mortality trends in high income countries. Nevertheless, conventional data sources to measure cause-specific mortality trends are affected by recurring changes in the International Classification of Diseases (ICD). They also lack the degree of detail needed to construct consistent time series, at least for the periods before implementation of the 10th ICD Revision.

uslaw-cfr-t40-s60-2055.title: 40 C.F.R. § 60.2055 — What is a waste management plan?
uslaw-cfr-t40-s60-2055.creator: Environmental Protection Agency
uslaw-cfr-t40-s60-2055.description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 40 (Protection of Environment), Part 60 (). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A waste management plan is a written plan that identifies both the feasibility and the methods used to reduce or separate certain components of solid waste from the waste stream in order to reduce or eliminate toxic emissions from incinerated waste.

uslaw-usc-t50-s213.title: 50 U.S.C. § 213 — Jurisdiction of confiscation proceedings
uslaw-usc-t50-s213.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t50-s213.description: United States Code, Title 50 (War And National Defense); Chapter 13 (Insurrection). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Such prizes and capture shall be condemned in the district court of the United States having jurisdiction of the amount, or in admiralty in any district in which the same may be seized, or into which they may be taken and proceedings first instituted.
